question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose the focused media-base64/media-mime Plugin SDK APIs and accept explicit local-root requirements plus strict malformed-data-URL rejection for existing WhatsApp media integrations?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but this choice fixes the permanent external Plugin SDK shape and deliberately changes compatibility and security-boundary behavior that tests alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept the canonical media contract
options.body: Approve the focused SDK exports and fail-closed media boundary, then merge with the documented strict parsing and explicit-root behavior.

options.title: Keep compatibility temporarily
options.body: Require a narrowly documented compatibility or migration plan for existing injected readers and plugin consumers before accepting the API change.

options.title: Pause the SDK expansion
options.body: Keep the WhatsApp cleanup local and defer new public media subpaths until an owner defines the desired external plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the canonical media contract
recommendation.body: Approve the focused SDK exports and fail-closed media boundary, then merge with the documented strict parsing and explicit-root behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies mcaxtr as the only concrete contributor across the affected WhatsApp/media and follow-up QA work; owner confidence remains limited without a completed current-main blame pass.
